newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Expatriates leave HK for Britain on luxury cruise.
newsitem.headline: Expatriates leave HK for Britain on luxury cruise.

text.p: A group of British expatriates sailed into the sunset of Britain's colonial era on Thursday, leaving Hong Kong for home aboard a luxury cruise liner.

To the sounds of bagpipes and brass and a mix of tears and cheers, 50 retired expatriate civil servants and their 70 dependents boarded the Oriana as one of the last batches of expatriate officers to leave by sea.

"Naturally I am sad. We've been here nearly 18 years. Well, my wife has of course been here since birth. So it's a sad occasion," said Roy Griffey, who has worked in the territory as a government lawyer for 18 years and married a Hong Kong woman.
Aboard the liner, some toasted a leisurely month-long voyage with champagne while others waved Hong Kong flags.
The bill for the expatriates' voyage was carried by Hong Kong taxpayers. At about HK$63,000 (US$8,140) per head, the expatriates' return voyages cost about HK$10 million annually.
The cruise option for retiring expatriate officers was introduced in 1972, but was not part of new contracts from December 1984 because of an outcry over the privilege.
Britain hands the colony back to China on July 1 after more than 150 years of colonial rule.
